children: has been ordered to expand and accelerate payments to consumers that were harmed by the e-commerce giant’s deceptive Prime enrollment practices.
Under the September 2025 settlement with the Federal Trade Commission (FTC), Amazon
agreed to refund consumers who used fewer than 10 Prime benefits during a one-year period $51 each. The settlement amounted to $1.5B in addition to another $1B civil penalty.
must refund customers who used between 11 and 20 Prime benefits during a one-year period with the maximum amount refunded increased to $200 from $51.
Last year, the FTC accused Amazon
of using deceptive methods to sign up millions of consumers for its Prime membership and making it "exceedingly" difficult to cancel.

“The evidence showed that Amazon used sophisticated subscription traps designed to manipulate consumers into enrolling in Prime and then made it exceedingly hard for consumers to end their subscription,” the September 2025 FTC complaint alleged.
Besides the increased payment amount and wider eligibility threshold, the revised order eliminates the need for eligible consumers to submit claims or additional paperwork to Amazon
